review_text_raw:
A story about an idiot surrounded by other idiots who sound like idiots.

At no point was there any reason to sympathize with Anna and her lifetime of bad decisions that got her into this mess. She's like the stereotypical white person in a horror movie whose phone suddenly goes to static and runs out of gas in the middle of the night in front of an obviously haunted house and says "I should investigate this immediately, and by myself!". Her dumbass ex, her dumbass new lover, her dumbass "best friend", all of whom supposedly want to help her yet they somehow form the main obstacles to doing so, especially the "best friend" who is basically a secondary antagonist for all the help she is. Aside from bit players like the completely unconvincing cop. I thought the cop was lying about being a cop and that that was important as first, but nope, just terrible voice acting, we're supposed to believe that's what cops sound like. Though he's not as bad as the villain revealed at the end, who sounds like a 13 year old boy who got his big brother to install voice changing software for him because he thinks it'll make him sound badass on voice chat while playing Halo. It's that bad. Was it supposed to be intimidating? Was it supposed to be a shocking reveal? It wasn't, just the annoying end to a nonsensical story about thoroughly unsympathetic idiots. Nothing about this is redeemable, this was a waste of a Humble Bundle pick. And they had the nerve to release a sequel? Why, because they can churn out terrible games like this once a week? I hope it at least has an "everyone dies" ending, because after meeting all of these characters, I honestly don't want any of them to live, it would be better for society for every one of them to go away.

This was my first "found phone" type of mystery/horror to play so I was quite intrigued by the concept and mechanics as a whole. It really challenged how well of a snoop you were sometimes. Hilariously, I kept getting all the bad choices that ultimately led me to getting probably the worst ending possible and I wasn't really upset by that. However, there were some aspects that were a bit troubling for me throughout my playthrough. 

The jumpscares were considerably louder than the rest of the game and there are no audio options available. I guess I could understand if that was intentional since the "investigation" periods are very quiet (aside from [spoiler]the random knocks which were genuinely terrifying because I thought they were happening IRL[/spoiler]), but I actually did have fun just snooping through/messing with Anna's phone and texting everyone, so the cheap jumpscares took me out of the game pretty often.

Also, the climax (and the ending as a whole) just didn't totally sit right with me for some reason. Maybe my focus was waning by that point, but with hardly enough exposition to help drive the antagonist's motives, it just felt very out of left field. (Okay, maybe if I hadn't gone into this game ≈99% blind and maybe had also known [spoiler]what a simulacrum was[/spoiler], I would've had a better idea of what I was getting myself into.) With all that being said, I was left feeling underwhelmed and unsatisfied.

At the end of the day, SIMULACRA was [b]just okay[/b]. It's already very cheap in price, but I recommend you buy it during a sale if you're really that interested. I have just a small shred of hope for improvement on the second game.

review_text_raw:
This game is a bit annoying. I kinda enjoyed my time with it but it's just not good.

On the plus side: it's got decent social media puzzles and a sufficiently creepy atmosphere, ... and that's about all it has going for it. On the minus side: The writing is terrible, the voice acting is not great, there are several cheap jump scares, and the story itself is awful.

Ooh, the story has multiple endings and I should play again? No thank you, once is enough. I can't see what the game could have to offer besides more weak dialogue and weird railroady decisions.

Spoilers, I guess, but I lost and got the worst ending because I didn't show enough trust in the sleazebag (who was specifically written as a sleazy dude) ALL THE WAY IN THE BEGINNING OF THE GAME. It always bunches my britches when a game does that: "Oh you didn't do a thing when you didn't have all the information yet and you couldn't make an informed decision about it? Sucks to be you, Anna's dead." Oh, and also Taylor, he's dead too. Just because I wouldn't send the sleazy dude a cute selfie of the missing girl and I wasn't sufficiently sad enough about him being caught with his pants down (literally, fuck, it's such a contrived story).

I feel like the game is less about saving Anna and more about how you're supposed to protect the feelings of the two douchebag brodudes. There's only one other recurring character, Anna's best friend, Ashley, who could have been of great help, but the story sidelines her almost immediately and only brings her back to intimate that she's secretly in love with Anna. Again, spoilers, but if you've read this far, I doubt you care. (edit: Reading someone else's review, I just learned that to get the absolute best ending, you have to catfish the best friend and reciprocate her feelings without Anna's consent or Ashley's knowledge. Cool game, bro!)

Anyway, don't bother with this game unless you really want a 5 hour puzzle game with a crappy story.

This is a tough call, especially given the price of the game. I'm going negative here because the "Overwhelmingly Positive" is out of line. This game is average, at best.

The concept itself is unique and the gameplay, for the most part, is well developed.

The main problem is the /r/nosleep storyline and unprofessional voice actors (especially Greg, I actually physically cringed when listening to his line deliveries). On top of that, there's some laughably blunt social commentary that's simply ridiculous. Someone else said it well, if they were going to be camp, they should have just gone all out campy horror. Instead, this is supposed to be serious and that's a shame.

Even more of a shame because the cryptology and detective stuff is really well done in this game. There's a lot of potential, and honestly, if you're that curious and can handle the bad acting and dumb direction the story takes, the measly 5% negative reviews aren't going to dissuade you from trying it out. 

But if you're on the fence, just look elsewhere.

review_text_raw:
Sad to say that I had to refund this. The premise seemed solid based on the store page - trying to piece together clues to someone's disappearance when you only have their phone - and the general interface was well done, but that was about it. My first hour of playing this mostly consisted of:

[list]
[*] Listening to overdramatic, very slowly worded voice messages.
[*] Piecing together "corrupted" pictures and texts that had absolutely nothing to do with Anna's disappearance. 
[*] Wondering if a proofreader was ever used for this game. Most of the articles and texts gave me the impression that English isn't the developer's first language. While I have nothing against that, coming across awkward grammar really took the immersion out of a mostly text-based game.
[*] Sitting through consecutive rounds of text-vomit finger-pointing from Greg and Taylor. I truly detest people who text at a rate of 50 messages/min when a single sentence would have sufficed. I didn't think it could get any worse, but in came the relationship drama...
[*] An overall disconnect between the gameplay and the plot. A girl disappears with clear hints of some non-human entity behind it, so why am I wasting my time investigating the sorry backgrounds of two garden-variety losers?
[/list]

Maybe the game gets better beyond the 1.7-hour point, but I really didn't have the patience to sit through constant notifications from the Male MC Idiot Express while waiting for some actual horror story to happen. Honestly, I'd have been happier to just shut the damn phone off and actually set out to find Anna door to door. At least then the "investigation" would have felt more productive.

review_text_raw: This game had a slate of good ideas executed poorly. There are a ton of grammar mistakes in the English version that make situations unclear, and make the actions of characters within the story seem unrealistic, or come out of nowhere. The writing seems to come from a very immature perspective that seems to commodify women as sex objects. A lot of the game seems to want you to comply with the demands of the male characters, while the sole female character that knew the victim is uncooperative and aggressive toward you. The game chastised me for failing to get a guy to trust me, because he lied about having information I needed and wanted me to send him a picture of the victim from her phone in exchange for said information he didn't have. And even though I told him that was creepy and he seemed to understand, he later blew up at me for it and got himself killed. There's no sense of accountability, consistency, or predictability in these incredibly unrealistic interactions, and if it weren't for the lacking in that area of writing (and the sometimes horrible voice acting -- I'm looking at you, Greg), this could have actually been a very compelling and immersive game. Instead, the lack of payoff and random interactions render it a complete waste of time.

review_text_raw:
The Good Stuff:

The layout and idea behind the game is pretty cool. I like how each "app" generally feels like a real app where you can do whatever, like comment of peoples posts or call random numbers. It is really neat design idea and it is well executed.

I also enjoyed a few of the more difficult puzzles, as they really added a sense of immersion into digging through someone's phone. The puzzles are mainly pretty easy, but the game doesn't baby you through them at all, so you feel smart when you manage to pull of something a bit more complicated.

The Bad Stuff:

For me, story is one of the most important parts of a game like this, and unfortunately SIMULACRA fails to deliver a good one.

Mild Spoilers: [spoiler]While the ending tried to be Black Mirror-esque, I feel like the story fails to properly set up the ending, so it kinda comes out of nowhere. Also, many things in the story aren't well explained or left to Deus Ex Machina[/spoiler]

There are multiple endings, and you will get an idea of what they all are when you finish the game. Some of the potential outcomes have me slightly curious, but not enough to replay it to see them. Perhaps the story would have been more interesting had I gotten a different ending.

I am not a huge fan of horror, but I have played games like Prey and Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice that have a creepy horror feel. The creepiness of SIMULACRA lasts only about the first 30 mins and then you become generally innoculated.

The main title song was also pretty cheesy.

As many other reviews have pointed out, some of the voice acting is on the level of "so bad it's hilarious".

I understand that with a smaller scale game like this it is difficult, but I felt like the chat options often strong-armed me into things I didn't want to say, which made things like [spoiler]gaining Taylor's trust[/spoiler] feel unfair.

The Bottom Line: If you want a game with a good story, there are better games. If you want a game where choices matter, there are better games. If you want a horror game, there are better games. If you just want to see a cool mechanic in action, then you might want to check it out.

Summary: For a horror/mystery/puzzle game, it is quite weak on each of the three elements. The least surprising mystery game I've played. Perhaps mainly because it blows its load from the start and spends the rest of the play time catching up with itself. Probably works better on mobile, as it seems made for a short attention span.

Pros:
- Basic concept is a cool commentary on social media and online dating
- A couple of surprising moments
- Some easter eggs and alternative paths give a bit of replay value

Cons:
- Storytelling is overstated and predictable
- Dialog is unconvincing, and I often didn't like my choices
- Game is linear and holds your hand almost the entire way. Some light puzzles, but otherwise no challenge, except unlocking a certain ending
- Acting is meh, supporting voice acting is mostly plain bad
- Annoying spelling errors are not always intentional

For examples of similar storytelling that really works: see Oxenfree and Doki Doki Literature Club.

I played the whole game because I wanted it to be good.

The ending section is way too long and heavy handed and as a result any horror is sapped out of it. The voice sections also feel like they're punishing you because you can't respond in any way so the first few just feel like you're getting yelled at for no reason.

I found the game interesting and would have loved to see it through,but i couldn't bring myself to finish it.

In other reviews it's mention that it might be a bit of a slog to get through,but i found the information gathering,while repetitive to be quite nice and clever.

What stops me if the sudden jumpscars,they are not telegraphed well (there is very little to no indication that a jumpscared will happen,no tension build up,none of that,one moment you are looking through apps and suddenly you're struck with a jumpsacre when returning to the homepage).

As someone who is quite sensitive to jumpscares,even already knowing about the fact that there were jumpscares,the first major one was what stopped me from wanting to play.If the jumpscares were more subtle and less horrific i think it would have been more possible for me to finish,or at least get further in.

Another issue i had was that the game had no way of changing the volume inside the game,and i had to change it manually on my computer,someone who is less technically literate would probably have gotten an unintended jumpscare from the sudden volume from purely opening the game

The voice acting (with greg specifically) any many dialog was unrealistic,but i foudn it to be a more enjoyable part of the game,as they contrasted the poorly executed jumpscares in levity,though i would understand if it was not the intended effect.

it is truly a shame,because using the mediums and technology for this kind of horror would have been truly wonderful,clever and thought provoking,and even if nihilistic,the story  (as far as i have heard in other's videos and such) and how it applies it's title to it's themes could have been great.

i might look into it's sequals,but i may simply not have the stomach to actually go through on playing them,i hope you have a lovely day :D

This game is really boring. It's a bunch of clicking buttons, along with some typing in of answers, and very light puzzle solving.
Really it's the story where the meat of the game is found, and it's extremely sub-par. I dunno if the author is someone who speaks English as a second language, but the writing is very much flawed, and the logical choices in story progression just don't add up. The story and choices are as limited as the writer is, and this one I find very much unenjoyable.

It focused far too much on a relationship that simply wouldn't happen in reality. That girl is way out of his league, and there's no way Greg and Anna would ever have seen each other. In addition the flirtation, and everything to do with interactions between people is extremely awkward. The voice acting reaches levels of cringe, and not the lel cringe lulz, but the physical reaction of cringing.

Everything about this game is mediocre, and I have no idea how it is sitting at "Overwhelmingly Positive". It is so very far from that, and I think this is people with low expectations due to not seeing much of this sort of thing. The bandwagon effect is also a possibility, as well as attraction to the girl, but whatever the reason, this game is not worth a recommendation.

The voice acting is terrible and feels very performative, rather than being believable phone calls/voice messages. The story is linear, and there isn't much room for creativity (e.g. sending people random pictures to see how they respond), and there aren't really any things to mess around with on the phone that are interesting. The puzzles are ridiculously simple and serve no purpose other than to slow down the narrative. The jump scares, if you consider them that, are pretty pointless and don't enhance the story or experience whatsoever. The writing is generally bad and unbelievable (e.g. [spoiler]the CEO of Phresh Ideas divulging way too much information [/spoiler]), and many of the dialog options do not make sense at all. The characters frequently go between texting and calling in a way that doesn't feel believable, and behave very strangely (e.g. [spoiler]at the end of the game, a character is literally texting you as he's pushing someone to their death off of a balcony [/spoiler]). After finishing the game you can go back through more quickly to see the alternate endings, but it still takes too long, and you still have to sit through a lot of dialogue at the end at the normal speed.

Ultimately I would not recommend purchasing this game, solely because the primary focus of this game is the narrative and it felt weak. I received this game from a bundle.
